connector: You’ve read five chapters. Today there’s nothing new to read, so you get to look back like a detective. Who has the harder life, Jemmy or the prince? Gather your clues from the whole story, then check your opinion one last time.

plate.alt: A painting of a lonely stone tower on a hill under a cloudy sky
plate.credit: Dolbadarn Castle (detail) · J. M. W. Turner, 1799–1800 · Public domain
plate.look: A real castle tower in Wales, painted by J. M. W. Turner more than 200 years ago. It stands alone on a hill, a little like the north tower where Jemmy sleeps.

a.raw: the king crossed his arms and muttered disgusting
a.fixed: The king crossed his arms and muttered, “Disgusting.”
a.why: The starts the sentence, so it gets a capital T. A comma comes before the quotation. Quotation marks go around the word the king says, and it starts with a capital D. The period goes inside the closing quotation mark.

b.raw: the tutor shook his head and sighed hopeless
b.fixed: The tutor shook his head and sighed, “Hopeless.”
b.why: The starts the sentence, so it gets a capital T. A comma comes before the quotation. Quotation marks go around the word the tutor says, and it starts with a capital H. The period goes inside the closing quotation mark.

vcloze1.h1: The prince almost never feels sorry. Which bank word means truly sorry?
vcloze1.why: contrite means feeling truly sorry for something wrong.

vcloze2.h1: Jemmy can’t believe his ears. Which bank word means great surprise?

vcloze3.h1: Billy grabs, threatens and sneers. Which bank word names that kind of person?
vcloze3.why: a ruffian is a rough, violent person.

vcloze4.h1: Jemmy is fed up with the prince. Which bank word means building frustration?
vcloze4.why: exasperation is frustration that keeps building.

match.contrite: Contrite is how you feel after doing wrong. Look for the meaning about feeling sorry.
match.astonishment: Astonishment is a big feeling of surprise. Look for that meaning.
match.ruffian: A ruffian is a kind of person, a rough one. Look for the bully meaning.
match.exasperation: Exasperation builds up when someone keeps bothering you. Look for the frustration meaning.

scholar.journal-q1: … and say which part you think Jemmy minds the most.
scholar.journal-q2: … and explain how the whipping boy rule lets the pranks keep going.
scholar.journal-q3: … and explain whether the other boy is also a little bit responsible.

wordgame.title: Up the North Tower
wordgame.sub: Jemmy’s little room is at the top. Every right answer lights a step.
wordgame.look: This is the north tower of the castle, where Jemmy sleeps. Tiny stairs zig-zag up the stone wall. You light 8 steps each day this week. On Day 4 you reach Jemmy’s window at the top.
wordgame.todo: Read the question. Tap the answer you think is right. A right answer lights the next step.
wordgame.win: Today’s 8 steps are lit. Come back next lesson to climb higher.
wordgame.winWeek: You reached Jemmy’s window at the top of the north tower!

miss.1: under is sub-. Look at how interrupt starts.

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: Jemmy was scared, ___ he kept walking.
items.why: but: scared and walking anyway push against each other.

miss.0: and just adds. These halves push against each other.
miss.2: so shows a result. Being scared doesn’t make you keep walking.

items.title: Split the word
items.why: rail · road keeps both teams, ai and oa, together.

miss.1: That split pulls the ai team apart.

items.title: Word parts
items.q: A boat that goes under the sea is a…

miss.1: interact starts with the part that means between.

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: The fog rolled in, ___ the boys got lost.
items.why: so: the fog is why they got lost.

miss.0: and just adds. Here one half causes the other.
miss.1: but shows a difference. Getting lost in fog makes sense.

items.title: Find the vowel team
items.q: Which word has a vowel team?
items.why: groan: oa makes the long o sound.

miss.1: crisp has just one vowel, i.

items.title: Word parts
items.q: A game played between many nations is…

miss.1: submarine starts with the part that means under.

glossary.m: a boy kept in the castle to be punished whenever the prince does something wrong
a joining word, like and, but, or so
two vowels side by side that make one sound, like ai in rain
one beat in a word. Rain-bow has two.
what you think, said in one clear sentence

transcripts.welcome: Welcome back, it’s Opti. Today we look back at all five chapters. One boy has fine clothes and a king for a father. The other has rags and a lot of whacks. So here’s the big question: who really has the harder life? Hold on to your answer, because today you’ll check your whole opinion from top to bottom.
transcripts.guide1: Word study review day. You’ll roll some dice, fix joining words that don’t fit, and fill in sentences with words from all week. When something feels tricky, think back to Day 1. The patterns haven’t changed. You’ve just gotten better at spotting them.
transcripts.guide2: No new chapters today. Instead, think back over the whole story so far. Picture the feast, the tower, the fog, and the outlaws. Which moment tells you the most about the prince? Which one tells you the most about Jemmy? Keep those two moments in mind.
transcripts.guide3: Time to be your own editor. Read your claim, your reason, and your example out loud. Does each part do its job? Does your example really prove your reason? Find one thing to make stronger. Even great writers fix their work before anyone else reads it.

notes.wordParts: inter- means “between” (interrupt, interact, international). sub- means “under” (submarine).
notes.grammar: A conjunction is a joining word. and adds an idea, but shows a difference, and so shows a result.
notes.spelling: A vowel team is two vowels that make one sound, like ai in rain. A team stays together in one syllable: rain·bow, sea·son.
notes.wgrd: Good readers step back and think about the whole section: who suffers more, and does either character deserve our sympathy?
vocab: feeling truly sorry for something wrong you did
complete surprise; unable to believe what you see
a rough, violent person; a bully or criminal
strong frustration that has been building up
